note: FNS Section 1066 is entirely a QC variance determination procedure — it describes how a QC reviewer must evaluate a case when a household has more than one TYPE of income (earned, unearned, annualized/prorated). The Comparison I / Comparison II framework is audit methodology: Comparison I tests total income against the allotment, and Comparison II requires the reviewer to evaluate each income type separately using type-specific procedures from Sections 1062-1065. This has no caseworker equivalent. The underlying substantive policy — that different income types exist, each has its own rules, and all countable income is added together — IS covered in the OLG across multiple pages: 'How SNAP Benefits are Calculated' (Step One: 'Add together the household's countable earned and unearned income'), 'Types of Earned Income' (wages, steady employment, income averaging, mandatory annualization), 'Unearned Income Overview', and BEACON data entry procedures for each income type. The OLG adequately guides workers on handling multiple income types; the Comparison I/II QC review framework is not something caseworkers need.
